values.note: $26 a night for a single site (2026, 2027 and 2028 rate tables), $50 for a double site. One camping unit per site; an extra vehicle is $8 a night if not added to the reservation.

fees.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232001/rates (Peak Season 2026-05-22..09-12 and 2027-05-21..09-11, First-come First-served Season 2026/2027: 'STANDARD NONELECTRIC': 26) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/hiawatha/recreation/flowing-well-campground ('Single Campsite: $26 per night', 'Double Campsite: $50 per night') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232001 (notice: 'Extra vehicle will be charged an $8 per night fee'), read 2026-10-25

hookups.source: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 232001 (all 6 sites typed STANDARD NONELECTRIC), read 2026-10-25

values.note: The recreation.gov catalog lists 6 standard sites (4 reservable, 2 first-come), each for an RV, trailer or tent to 25 ft; 4 are pull-throughs. The pages call it 'less than a dozen spacious sites'.

sites.source: recreation.gov campsite catalog for 232001 (Max Vehicle Length 25 on all 6; Driveway Entry: 4 Pull-Through, 2 Back-In) + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232001 ('The campground offers less than a dozen spacious sites for tent and RV camping'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Well water with heavy iron and sulfur content ('an acquired taste, but is safe to consume'). The Forest Service page currently reports a temporary water outage (bring all water, including drinking water). recreation.gov lists accessible vault toilets; the Forest Service page says 'Restrooms are not available at this site.'

facilities.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/hiawatha/recreation/flowing-well-campground ('Potable water is available at this site'; Current Conditions: 'Our facility is experiencing a temporary water outage. Please bring all the water you'll need for your visit, including drinking water.'; 'Restrooms are not available at this site.') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232001 ('Accessible vault toilets and drinking water are provided'), read 2026-10-25

values.note: Reserve on recreation.gov or (877) 444-6777; 2 of the 6 sites are first-come only, and the rate table opens each season with a first-come week in mid-May (2027: May 14-20). Reservations close 4 days before arrival. A reserved site is held until noon the day after arrival. Check-in 2 pm.

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/232001 (rules maxConsecutiveStay 14, reservationCutOff 4, minWeekendStay 0; notices on holding sites and check-in) + catalog (2 sites reservable: false) + /rates ('First-come, First-served Season' 2027-05-14..05-20) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/hiawatha/recreation/flowing-well-campground ('Visit Recreation.gov or call (877) 444-6777'), read 2026-10-25

note: Small Hiawatha NF campground on the west bank of the Sturgeon River, 2.8 miles north of US-2 on Forest Highway 13 (east of Rapid River). Spacious sites, some along the bank overlooking the slow-moving river; group picnic area. The Sturgeon River Canoe Trail runs through the campground. --Claude
summary: recreation.gov API/rates/catalog + FS page: confirmed $26 (2026-2027), no electric, reservable on recreation.gov. Changed site count 10 -> 6 (catalog; pages say 'less than a dozen'); new max_rig_ft 25 with 4 pull-throughs, season May 15 - Sept 15 (FS 'Seasons of Use'), fcfs some_sites, 14-night max. Vault toilets left as is (rec.gov yes, FS page says no restrooms). Note trimmed of field restatements.
flags: Water: the Forest Service page's Current Conditions report 'a temporary water outage. Please bring all the water you'll need for your visit, including drinking water.' The page also shows 'Site Closed', which matches the end of its May 15 - September 15 season.
Phone: the entry's 906-474-6442 (Rapid River/Manistique Ranger District) matches the FS page; recreation.gov's contact line instead says 'please call (906) 767-1111'.

Operator: recreation.gov marks it not commercially managed, but its refund notice speaks of 'the campground concessionaire' and 'the campground manager'; the FS page names no concessionaire. Ownership federal stands either way.

Waterfront re-audit lead: the entry is 'riverview', but recreation.gov and the FS page say 'Some sites are situated along the bank, overlooking the slow-moving river' (a riverbank-site claim; waterfront not changed).
Restrooms: recreation.gov says 'Accessible vault toilets ... are provided'; the Forest Service page says 'Restrooms are not available at this site.'
